multicolor.description: Groups only: show every part in its own colour (Tinkercad's Multicolor) instead of the group colour.

groupResize.description: Groups and bundles only: what the group does with its parts when it is resized (Discussion #526). stretch (the default) stretches them all with it. keepParts stretches only the parts that reach across at least nine tenths of the group along the axis that changes (the plate, a wall, the hollow of a box), keeping their distance to both sides; every other part keeps its own size and its distance to the nearer side, and a centred one stays centred - so the corner holes of a plate made longer stay round and where they were. A part the group becomes too small for shrinks with it after all. Applies to every later resize (width, depth, height here, scale_objects, the handles) and, set on a group that is stretched already, at once; the answer comes after the group is built again. A mirrored, tapered or deformed group, or one with fillets, chamfers or a texture of its own, stretches everything.

rotationPivot.description: The point this body turns about, in workplane coordinates like x, z and elevation. It stays with the body: it moves, turns and scales with it, and the rotate handle and R key turn the body about it. null removes it.

shapeLocked.description: Lock shape (#1277), the second level of locking: the object can still be moved, turned, lifted, aligned, copied and grouped with others, but its size, its settings, its name and its body stay as they are - no resizing, ungrouping, mirroring, edge tools or deleting, and a group holding such a part keeps its size. A copy keeps the lock. While it is on, update_object takes only x, z, elevation, rotation, rotationX, rotationZ, rotationPivot, hidden, transparent and locked; pass shapeLocked: false in the same call to change anything else.

edge.description: Extruded sketch bodies with align outside, inside or center: a cutting edge, the width in mm the wall's top runs in to with a 45° chamfer on both sides (a cookie cutter's wall); 0 for a flat top, and an edge as wide as the line or wider is none.

stroke.description: Extruded sketch bodies (an imported SVG among them) and texts: how the body is filled. An object builds the outline as a frame - align outside is Tinkercad's outer line, inside its inner line, center on the line - or with align grow keeps the area and widens it by width all round; width in mm; join miter (sharp), round or bevel; edge a cutting edge on top of a sketch body's wall; values left out keep the current ones. null makes it a filled area again. A sketch body is built again from its sketch, where it stands; a text keeps its letters and its box grows by the stroke's reach (outside and grow by width, center by half).

silhouette.description: Extruded sketch bodies and texts: true leaves out every outline inside another - holes, and islands in them; on a text the counters of its letters - false brings them back. With an outside stroke this makes a cookie cutter from one SVG; with grow, a base layer under a text.

sketchOperation.description: Sketch bodies only: make the body again from its sketch as another kind - an imported SVG comes in extruded, revolve turns its outline about the sketch's vertical axis (x = 0) into a round body, as the sketch's badge does in the editor. The new body keeps the id, name and colour and stands where the old one stood, its foot at the same height; an extrusion made from another kind is 10 mm high. Edge treatments go. For a revolve an outline reaching across the axis is first moved left until its right edge lies on it, so the half cross-section of an SVG turns about its straight side; sweep needs a construction line as the path.

revolveSmoothness.description: Exact revolved sketch bodies only (Discussion #1426): how finely the round faces are cut into facets, as the Smoothness field sets it. standard: within 0.05 mm and about 9 degrees; fine: 0.02 mm and 4.6 degrees; extraFine: 0.01 mm and 2.3 degrees, for a large pot whose facets show on a print. Finer means more triangles. A helix or an older mesh revolve has sides instead and refuses it.

stretch.description: Straight text only: true stretches the letters to fill the whole box in both directions, so a capital can be made lower or narrower as in Tinkercad; false (the default) fits them into the box with their proportions kept, centred. Set the box with width and depth.

vertical.description: true stacks the letters top to bottom, each centred on one upright line. Straight text: the box turns upright and the letters keep their size. Curved text: the column runs along the circle of textRadius, its middle at the circle's left side (textInward: the right side), the letters standing upright, so a name follows the rim of a disk; textFlipped does nothing then. Spacing widens or narrows the gap between the letters.

spacing.description: Text only: the space between the letters on top of the font's own, in per cent of the letter size - 0 as the font has it, above it wider, below it tighter (down to -50), up to 300. Straight and curved text; the letters keep their size and the box follows. Not applied to Arabic and Hebrew, whose letters join up.

kerning.description: Text only: automatic kerning - true moves pairs of letters that leave too much room between them (AY, AV, LT, To) closer, measured from the letters' shapes, in every font; false sets every letter at the font's own width. New texts start with it on, texts made before it existed have it off. Straight and curved text; the letters keep their size and the box follows. Not for vertical text, Arabic, Hebrew or Japanese.

letterWidth.description: Curved text only: how wide each letter is drawn, in per cent of its own width - 100 as the font has it, below narrower (down to 25), above wider (up to 400). The letters keep their height and the arc they take grows or shrinks with them; the box follows. For straight text use stretch with width and depth instead.

size.description: How wide and high the edge is, in mm (0.05 to 5, at most the text's height).

letterEdge.description: Text only: the top edge of the letters rounded or chamfered, as the top layer of a name tag is finished. null takes it off. Built from the outline stepped inwards, so it works for every font and word; the edge tool takes such a text as a mesh.

sides.description: Cylinder, slot, cone, curved cone, tube, polygon, pyramid, round roof, teardrop, counterbore, countersink, doubleCountersink, torus (around the ring). Left out on a round body, the side count follows the diameter.

steps.description: Sphere and half sphere: how finely the surface is divided. Torus: how finely the tube is divided; left out, it follows the size.

bevel.description: Tube: wall thickness. Text: rounding of the lettering.

segments.description: Text only: steps in the rounding.

topRadius.description: Cone only: radius of the flat top. 0 runs to a point.

baseRadius.description: Cone only: radius at the base.

curvedConeTop.description: Curved cone only: the top's diameter as a share of the bottom's (the width), 0 to 1; 0 runs to a point, 1 is a cylinder. Default 0.25.

curvedConeBend.description: Curved cone only: how far the side bends, -1 to 1. Negative bends it inward into a trumpet like a pseudosphere, 0 is a straight cone, positive bulges it outward into a dome with a flat top. Default -0.8.

screwBossFastener.description: Screw boss only: what goes into its hole - a heat-set insert (default), a self-tapping screw for plastics, or a hole of your own (screwBossHole and screwBossHoleDepth).

screwBossSize.description: Screw boss only: the size from the fastener's list. Inserts: M2, M2.5, M3, M3S (short), M4, M5, #2-56, #4-40, #6-32, #8-32, #10-24, 1/4-20 (M3: hole 4.0 mm, insert 5.7 mm). Self-tapping screws: ST2.2, K25, ST2.9, K30, ST3.5, K40, ST4.2, K50, #2, #4, #6, #8, #10 (pilot hole 0.8 times the screw). Default M3, or K30 for screws.

screwBossHole.description: Screw boss only: the hole's diameter in mm, instead of the size's.

screwBossHoleDepth.description: Screw boss only: the hole's depth from the top in mm, instead of the size's (an insert's length + 1); as deep as the post goes through.

screwBossDiameter.description: Screw boss only: the post's outer diameter in mm (about twice an insert's hole, 2.5 times a screw). With gussets the width and depth are the footprint they reach to.

screwBossGussets.description: Screw boss only: thin ribs from the post down to the floor, 0 to 6 (default 0); they reach out to the footprint (width), screwBossGussetHeight high (default 0.6 of the post) and screwBossGussetThickness thick (1.6 mm).

screwBossGussetHeight.description: Screw boss only: how high the gussets reach up the post, mm.

screwBossGussetThickness.description: Screw boss only: the gussets' thickness, mm.

snapFitPart.description: Snap-fit only: both (default) puts the hook and its catch where they sit snapped in under a lid on top - the hook's foot at the top (under the lid), its barb at the bottom, the catch's back at +z (the inside of the wall it goes on); hook or catch makes one of them. separate_parts splits both into two bodies.

snapFitThickness.description: Snap-fit only: the arm's thickness, mm (1.6). The answer's strain at the root is 1.5 * thickness * undercut / length^2: PLA up to about 2 %, PETG and ABS about 4 %.

snapFitUndercut.description: Snap-fit only: how far the barb reaches under the catch, mm (1).

snapFitClearance.description: Snap-fit only: the play between barb and catch, mm (0.2, or the printer's play when one is set with layerling_printer_play).

snapFitLeadAngle.description: Snap-fit only: the barb's entry slope, degrees from the direction it goes in, 10-60 (30 slides in easily).

snapFitRetainAngle.description: Snap-fit only: the angle of the face that holds, 30-90: 90 holds for good, 45 lets it be pulled apart again.

snapFitFoot.description: Snap-fit only: the foot's thickness under the arm, mm (1.6; 0: no foot).

ribStyle.description: Rib only: a straight rib (width its length, depth its thickness) or a gusset, a right triangle that braces a wall against the floor (width along the floor, height up the wall at -x, depth its thickness). On a foot (ribFoot) the depth is the foot's width and ribThickness the rib's.

ribFoot.description: Rib only: true stands it on a foot, a thin plate under its whole length (a gusset: under its leg along the floor), centred under it and wider than it, for more hold on the bed or the floor so a thinner rib still stands; false takes it off again. Off by default. The box takes the foot in: depth is then the foot's width, ribThickness the rib's own, height still the whole height with the foot at its bottom. Switching it on keeps the rib as thick as it was (a new rib: 1.6 mm) unless ribThickness is given, and makes depth three times that unless depth is given; switching it off makes depth the rib's thickness again.

ribThickness.description: Rib on a foot (ribFoot) only: the rib's own thickness in mm; the foot (depth) reaches out at least 0.4 mm beside it on each side and widens with it where it would not.

ribFootThickness.description: Rib on a foot (ribFoot) only: the foot's thickness from the bottom in mm (0.8, four layers of 0.2), at least 0.2 and at most half the height.

ribFootShape.description: Rib on a foot (ribFoot) only: square (default, the foot's corners square) or oval, an ellipse seen from above with no corners to lift off the bed, centred under the rib, as wide as depth and just long enough that at the rib's ends it still reaches out by the rib's thickness from its middle (a gusset: half an ellipse from the wall past the tip). Its length is the box's width, the rib inside it shorter: 1 / sqrt(1 - (ribThickness / (depth / 2))^2) times, at most 1.5 times unless the foot is so narrow that its ends would stand on less than half of what the foot reaches out in the middle. Switching the shape, the foot, depth or ribThickness keeps the rib as long as it was and moves the width with it (a gusset's box grows away from its wall), unless width is given; a new oval rib is 40 mm long in a longer box.

topWidth.description: Pyramid only: width of the flat top. 0 runs to a point.

topDepth.description: Pyramid only: depth of the flat top. 0 runs to a point.

taperTopWidth.description: Taper, on every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: width of the top face. Setting one value of a face pins the other.

taperTopDepth.description: Taper, on every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: depth of the top face.

taperBottomWidth.description: Taper, on every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: width of the bottom face.

taperBottomDepth.description: Taper, on every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: depth of the bottom face.

extrudeTwist.description: On every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: rotates the top face relative to the base, in degrees, for a twisted extrusion.

extrudeTopOffsetX.description: On every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: shifts the top face along the shape's own X axis, in mm, for a leaning extrusion.

extrudeTopOffsetZ.description: On every shape except gear, hirth, pulley, thread, spring, gridfinity, hinge, pyramid, bentTube, teardrop, counterbore, countersink and ruler: shifts the top face along the shape's own Z axis, in mm, for a leaning extrusion.

slopeEnd.description: Box, roundedBox, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube, ring, wedge and roundRoof only: slope along - the height of the top at the lower end, in mm (0.2 up to the body's height); the other end keeps the body's height. Equal to the height means no slope.

slopeSide.description: Where slopeEnd applies: which end goes down (a round roof or a wedge slopes front or back only).

slopeCurve.description: Slope along only, where slopeEnd applies: how the top runs down to slopeEnd, -1 to 1: 0 straight, above 0 bulging up (level at the high end), below 0 sagging (level at the low end).

slopeFrom.description: Slope along only, where slopeEnd applies: where the top line starts - at one end (the default, the other end low), in the middle (both ends low, symmetric; slopeSide then only picks the axis) or "arch" (the slope stays and slopeCurve arches it evenly around its own middle).

sideDrop.description: Box, roundedBox, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube, ring, wedge and roundRoof only: side drop - how many mm the two longer sides are lowered at their edges, evenly, with the middle keeping the full height (0 for none, up to the height minus 0.2). Adds to a slope.

sideCurve.description: Side drop only, where sideDrop applies: how the top runs from the middle to the edges, -1 to 1: 0 straight, above 0 bulging up (a dome, level in the middle), below 0 sagging (level at the edges).

narrowEnd.description: Box, roundedBox, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, wedge and roundRoof only (not tube or ring): narrow along - seen from above, the width of the narrow end in mm (0 for a point, up to the full width); both long sides run in evenly so the end stays in the middle. The full width means no narrowing.

narrowSide.description: Where narrowEnd applies: which end narrows (a round roof or a wedge narrows front or back only).

narrowCurve.description: Narrow along only, where narrowEnd applies: how the sides run in to narrowEnd, -1 to 1: 0 straight, above 0 bulging out (a rounded bow), below 0 drawn in.

narrowStart.description: Narrow along only, where narrowEnd applies: where the narrowing starts, as a share of the length from the wide end, 0 to 0.95 (0.5 starts it in the middle).

teeth.description: Gear: how many teeth, 6 to 150. Hirth joint: how many teeth round the ring, 6 to 90 (default 24). GT2 pulley: how many teeth, 10 to 200 (default 20); with the fixed 2 mm pitch they set its diameter (outside diameter = teeth x 2 / pi - 0.508 mm).

gearProfile.description: Gear only: involute teeth that mesh (new gears), round teeth made of arcs (like Tinkercad's Useful gear: forgiving on small printed gears, a smooth grip on knobs), or the plain straight teeth older designs have. An involute gear's width and depth are its outside diameter, module x (teeth + 2): for module 1.5 and 20 teeth give width and depth 33. Round teeth stand lower, so a round gear's outside diameter is module x (teeth + 1.2): module 1.5 and 20 teeth give 31.8. Two gears with the same module and tooth shape mesh at a centre distance of module x (teeth1 + teeth2) / 2; gearBacklash applies to both, gearPressureAngle only to involute teeth.

gearPressureAngle.description: Involute gear only: pressure angle in degrees, 14.5 to 30 (default 20).

gearBacklash.description: Involute gear only: play of a meshing pair in mm, half taken off each gear (default 0.2, 0 for an exact gear).

toothSize.description: Gear with simple teeth only. Hirth joint: the teeth's height at the rim in mm, crest over root (default: right-angled teeth, pi x radius / teeth); up to the joint's full height, the roots then reach the bottom at the rim.

centerHoleSize.description: Gear, Hirth joint and GT2 pulley: bore through the middle (Hirth joint default 10, pulley default 5, 0 for none).

pulleyBeltWidth.description: GT2 pulley only: width of the toothed band between the flanges in mm, 1 to 100 (default 7, for a 6 mm belt; about 11 for a 10 mm belt). The pulley's height is flange + belt width + flange + hub; width, depth and height follow from its measures and cannot be set directly.

pulleyFlange.description: GT2 pulley only: thickness of each of the two flanges that keep the belt on, in mm, 0 to 10 (default 1, 0 for none).

pulleyFlangeRise.description: GT2 pulley only: how far the flanges reach past the teeth, in mm, 0.5 to 20 (default 1.5).

pulleyHubHeight.description: GT2 pulley only: height of the hub on top, in mm, 0 to 100 (default 6, 0 for none). For a set screw, cut a hole cylinder through the hub.

pulleyHubDiameter.description: GT2 pulley only: diameter of the hub, in mm (default 12); it stays within the flanges, or within the tooth roots without flanges.

hirthSteepFlank.description: Hirth joint only: saw teeth like a ratchet. The steep flank's angle to the face at the rim, 45 to 90 degrees (90 is a straight step); the other flank takes the rest of the tooth. Left out, the teeth are symmetric; 0 makes them symmetric again. A copy turned over front to back still locks into it.

hirthReverse.description: Hirth joint with saw teeth only: puts the steep flank on the other side of each tooth, so the ratchet holds the other way round.

gearType.description: Gear only. "herringbone" is two helical halves turning opposite ways, like an arrow: it centres itself on its shaft and has no axial thrust, which is why it suits 3D printing; it takes the same helixAngle and helixQuality as a helical gear, and two meshing herringbone gears have angles of opposite sign. "internal" is a ring gear with its teeth pointing in, the outer wheel of a planetary set: width and depth are its outside diameter, module x (teeth + 2.5) + 2 x gearRim (round teeth: module x (teeth + 1.7)), and a pinion of the same module meshes inside it at a centre distance of module x (teeth - pinion teeth) / 2; ring teeth = sun teeth + 2 x planet teeth. "rack" is a bar along x with its teeth towards +z: width = teeth x pi x module (so racks of one module line up end to end), depth the bar's thickness, free above the teeth plus 0.5; a gear of the same module rolls on it with its centre teeth x module / 2 in front of the pitch line, which lies a module behind the tooth tips. Both take involute or round teeth, never simple ones, and no centerHoleSize.

gearRim.description: Ring gear only: the rim outside the teeth, in mm (default 3).

helixAngle.description: Helical and herringbone gear only. With involute teeth the true helix angle on the pitch circle: two helical gears mesh with the same module and angle, one positive and one negative; with simple teeth the turn from foot to top.

bevelHelixAngle.description: Bevel gear only (-45 to 45, default 0): turns the teeth while they taper, a spiral bevel gear; computed like helixAngle, with helixQuality for how finely the turn is drawn. A spiral bevel gear stays a triangle mesh: no fillets, no STEP.

helixQuality.description: Helical, herringbone and spiral bevel gear only.

threadRole.description: Thread only. A bore becomes a cutter that threads the part it is grouped with.

threadHead.description: Thread only. For a screw the head: cylinder (socket head), countersunk, hex, square, flange (a hex with a disc under it), wing (a hub with a flat bar across, turned by hand, prints lying flat) or knob (a star knob with six lobes). For a nut its shape: hex (also for cylinder or countersunk), square, flange, wing or knob, sized from the thread (a wing nut 5 times the thread across, a star knob nut 5 times).

threadProfile.description: Thread only: tooth shape. "v" is the sharp 60-degree ISO default (M, UNC, UNF); trapezoidal and round both leave a flat crest and root, which prints more reliably; "whitworth" is the 55-degree profile with rounded crest and root of the G pipe threads (ISO 228-1); "custom" is a symmetric trapezoid whose depth and flank angle you set with threadDepth and threadFlankAngle.

threadTaper.description: Thread only: tapered 1 in 16 on the diameter, as the pipe thread NPT; false or missing is a straight thread. threadDiameter is then the wide end's. A rod or screw narrows towards its tip at the top; a nut or tapped hole widens towards its mouth at the top, so a tapered rod turned upside down screws into it. Any profile can be tapered; an NPT threadSize sets it.

threadDiameter.description: Thread only, in millimetres: 6 is an M6, 20.955 a G1/2 pipe thread. Width and depth follow it, they are not set separately. For a standard size, threadSize is simpler.

threadPitch.description: Thread only, in millimetres: an M6 runs 1.0 as standard. With threadStarts above 1 it is the distance from one thread to the next (it sets the profile's depth); each thread then climbs threadPitch times threadStarts a turn.

threadStarts.description: Thread only (#1348): threads side by side, as on a lead screw, 1 (default) to 8, and a lead (threadPitch times this) of at most half the circumference. A T8x8 lead screw is threadDiameter 8, threadPitch 2, threadStarts 4, threadProfile trapezoidal; a T8x2 is the same with 1. A standard size (threadSize) and a tapered thread have one start: threadSize sets it back to 1 unless the call sets it.

threadClearance.description: Thread only, for nuts and tapped holes: how much room the thread leaves so a printed pair still turns, across the diameter (0.4, or twice the printer's play when one is set with layerling_printer_play).

threadAxialClearance.description: Thread only, for nuts and tapped holes: extra play along the axis (mm, 0 to 1 but at most a fifth of the pitch, default 0): each tooth of the part gets this much thinner while the diameter stays. Add it to a small threadClearance for a thread that turns freely without rattling sideways.

threadDepth.description: Thread only, with threadProfile "custom": the thread depth in millimetres, outer minus core radius, so the core diameter is threadDiameter minus twice this. Default is the V thread's depth at the pitch (0.54 of it); at least a tenth of the pitch, at most 40 % of the diameter, and not so deep that the two flanks would take more than nine tenths of the pitch at the flank angle.

threadFlankAngle.description: Thread only, with threadProfile "custom": the angle between the two flanks of a tooth in degrees, 10 to 90, default 60 (the V thread; 30 is a trapezoid thread). At 90 or less no flank is flatter than 45 degrees to the horizontal, so the thread prints without supports.

threadBoltClearance.description: Thread only, for rods and screws: how much thinner in diameter (mm, 0 to 1, default 0) the bolt is built, so a printed bolt fits a metal nut. Try 0.2 to 0.3.

threadQuality.description: Thread only: columns around the circumference.

threadChamfer.description: Thread only: the break at the ends that leads the first turn in. On a nut, tapped hole and rod it is the top end (and the bottom end too, unless threadChamferBottom is given); on a screw it is the tip. On a nut or tapped hole the 45 degree cone reaches down to the thread core.

threadChamferBottom.description: Thread only, for a rod, nut or tapped hole: the chamfer at the bottom end when it should differ from the top one. Left out, the bottom end has threadChamfer. A screw has no chamfer there.

threadHeadHeight.description: Thread only, and only for a screw: height of the head. Left out it follows the standard for the size.

threadHeadChamfer.description: Thread only, and only for a screw with a cylinder or hex head: the chamfer that breaks the sharp rim of the head. 0 leaves it sharp.

threadHeadDiameter.description: Thread only, and only for a screw with a cylinder, hex, square, flange, wing or knob head: the head diameter, across flats on a hex, square or flange head, the span of a wing head, the diameter of a star knob (3 to 8 times the thread; 5 by default), in mm. Left out it follows the standard for the size. A countersunk head's diameter follows its height (90 degree cone).

threadDrive.description: Thread only, and only for a screw: the drive recess in the head. "hex" is a hex socket (the default for cylinder and countersunk heads), "torx" six lobes, "phillips" a cross, "slot" a straight slot across the head (for a flat screwdriver or a coin), "robertson" a square socket (the Robertson drive common in Canada), "none" a plain head turned by hand or with a spanner (the default for a hex head).

threadDriveSize.description: Thread only, for a screw with a drive, in mm: hex socket across flats, Torx outer diameter, or the span of the Phillips cross, or the slot's length (its width is a fifth of it), or the Robertson square across flats. Left out it follows the standard for the size (an M4 takes 3 mm hex, about T20, about PH2, Robertson #2 (2.84 mm); a slot runs as far across the head as it fits); it must fit the head.

threadDriveDepth.description: Thread only, for a screw with a drive: how deep the recess goes into the head, in mm, at most 90 % of the head height. 0 leaves the head without a drive. Left out it is 60 % of the head height, at most a little over half the diameter.

threadCollarHeight.description: Thread only, for a screw without a countersunk head or for a nut: the height of a round collar, in mm - between a screw's head and its thread (a spacer under a star knob, a shoulder under a head), or on a nut's top face. 0 or left out: none. Without a height of its own the thread keeps its length (a nut its body) and the shape grows by the collar.

threadCollarDiameter.description: Thread only, for a screw or nut with a collar: its diameter in mm, at least 0.4 mm wider than a screw's thread (a nut's: 1.3 times the thread plus 0.4 mm) and 0.4 mm narrower than the head or nut where it is narrowest (between a star knob's scallops, a wing head's hub, a nut's flats). Left out it is twice the thread.

springTurns.description: Spring only: turns of the coil, or the bends of a flat spring.

springWire.description: Spring only: thickness of the wire, or the width of a flat spring's band.

springForm.description: Spring only: coil (default) or flat - a band that runs in waves across the plate, width its length, depth how far the waves reach, height its thickness. A new flat spring is 60 x 16 x 4 mm unless sizes are given; switching an existing spring keeps its size, so give the new width, depth and height with it.

springPattern.description: Flat spring only: round waves (default), a zigzag or square turns.

springEnds.description: Flat spring only: an eye with a hole at each end (default), a tab across each end, or plain ends.

springHand.description: Spring only: winding direction; right-hand (default) like a usual compression spring, or left-hand.

starPoints.description: Star only: number of points or rays (3 to 32).

starInnerSize.description: Star only: diameter of the inner valleys in mm.

starOuterFillet.description: Star only: fillet radius at outer tips in mm.

starInnerFillet.description: Star only: fillet radius at inner valleys in mm.

starQuality.description: Star only: quality / segment count for fillet rounding (4 to 48).

heartTipFillet.description: Heart only: fillet radius at the bottom tip in mm (0 to 20).

heartQuality.description: Heart only: quality / segment count for lobe and tip rounding (16 to 64).

crescentThickness.description: Crescent only: thickness at the crescent center in mm.

crescentTipFillet.description: Crescent only: fillet radius at horn tips in mm (0 to 8).

crescentQuality.description: Crescent only: quality / segment count for arc and tip rounding (16 to 64).

knurlPattern.description: Knurl only: "straight" grooves along the axis (default; an exact CAD body, so the edge tool works on it), "diamond", two slanted rows crossing into small diamonds (a mesh), or "round", straight grooves and ridges as a smooth wave of arcs, a pleasant grip for knobs (an exact body; its depth stays below 0.45 of the pitch round the grip). A knurl is a round grip: width is the diameter (depth follows), height the length.

knurlCount.description: Knurl only: number of grooves around the grip, 6 up to what fits at a 0.8 mm pitch around the diameter, at most 180 (default 30).

knurlDepth.description: Knurl only: depth of a groove in mm, 0.1 up to a third of the radius (default 0.6).

knurlAngle.description: Diamond knurl only: angle of the grooves to the axis in degrees, 10 to 60 (default 30).

knurlChamfer.description: Knurl only: 45-degree chamfer on both ends in mm (default 0.5, 0 for none), at most a quarter of the diameter and just under half the height. Straight and round knurling stay an exact body with it.

hingeKnuckles.description: Hinge only: how many knuckles share the axis, odd from 3 to 15 (default 5) so the part with the pin holds both ends. A hinge is a print-in-place hinge lying open flat: width is its length along the axis (x), depth both leaves together (z), height the knuckle diameter; it prints in one piece and turns afterwards.

tubeBoreHole.description: Tube, ring or bent tube with an opening: when true the bore counts as a hole once the shape is grouped, so it also cuts the wall of whatever the tube is grouped with - two tubes in a T-junction open into each other. false or left out: the bore only keeps the tube hollow.

hingeKnuckleWidth.description: Hinge only: the knuckles are at most this wide in mm and their number follows (odd, from 3 up to 31), instead of giving hingeKnuckles; the fewest knuckles that are not wider. Left out, hingeKnuckles stands. Giving hingeKnuckles in a later update takes the width away.

hingeStyle.description: Hinge only: "pin" (default) puts a printed pin through the knuckles; "liftOff" makes two knuckles, the lower one carrying the pin to the end and the upper one a sleeve that lifts off it (a lift-off door hinge; the knuckle count is ignored); "pinless" leaves the pin out and runs the bore through every knuckle for a pin of one's own (the same as hingePinless true); "cone" gives every other knuckle cones on its ends that nest into conical recesses of the others - no pin and no bridge, so it prints lying flat without sagging. The cone hinge ignores hingePinDiameter, is an exact body like the others (chamfers and fillets work, true cones in STEP), makes fewer knuckles when they would be too short for a cone, and its hingeLeafThickness may be as thick as the whole knuckle (a flush hinge that opens about 90 degrees).

hingeConeSize.description: Hinge, cone style only: the diameter of a cone where it grows from its knuckle, in mm. Left out, the largest that fits; a larger value is cut back to that.

hingePinDiameter.description: Hinge only: diameter of the pin in mm (default 3); the other part's bore is wider by the clearance.

hingeLeafThickness.description: Hinge only: thickness of the two leaves in mm (default 2), at most the knuckle radius less the bore radius so a leaf stays below the bore.

hingeClearance.description: Hinge only: gap in mm between the moving parts (0.1 to 1, default 0.4) - around the pin, between the knuckles and in front of the leaves. Go up for a printer that tends to fuse, down for a tighter hinge.

hingePinless.description: Hinge only: leave the printed pin out. The bore (pin diameter plus the clearance) then runs through every knuckle, the ends included, for a pin of your own such as a piece of filament or wire (default false).

hingeAngle.description: Hinge only: fold the second leaf up about the pin, in degrees (-180 to 180, default 0): 0 lies flat as it prints, 180 is closed, below 0 it folds down past lying flat. Set it back to 0 before printing the hinge in place.

hingeScrewHoles.description: Hinge only: screw holes in each leaf along the axis, 0 to 6 (default 0, none). Fewer are made where fewer fit, each keeping 0.5 mm of leaf to the edges, the knuckles and the next hole.

hingeScrewDiameter.description: Hinge only: diameter of the screw holes in mm (1 to 12, default 3.5).

hingeScrewSpacing.description: Hinge only: from one screw hole's centre to the next along the axis, in mm. Left out or 0, the holes share the length evenly.

hingeScrewAcross.description: Hinge only: from the hole in one leaf to the hole in the other, across the axis, centre to centre, in mm. Left out or 0, each hole sits in the middle of its leaf beside the knuckles.

hingeScrewCountersink.description: Hinge only: countersink the screw holes at 90 degrees for countersunk screws, on the side that faces the other leaf when the hinge is closed (default true); false makes straight holes.

hingeScrewHead.description: Hinge only: the screw holes' top - countersunk at 90 degrees (default), straight, nut (a hexagonal pocket for a nut on top, the side facing the other leaf when closed) or countersunkNut (the back leaf, the one with the pin, countersunk and the front leaf with nut pockets). Takes the place of hingeScrewCountersink.

hingeNutWidth.description: Hinge only: the nut's width across the flats in mm for nut pockets, 0 or left out to take it from the hole's diameter (M3 5.8, M4 7.3 with play). The pocket is as deep as a nut is high, leaving 0.6 mm of leaf below it; on a leaf too thin for that it is left out.

hingeCornerRadius.description: Hinge only: round the four outer corners of the leaves with this radius in mm (default 0, sharp); with fingers, the two outer corners of each finger.

hingeLeafStyle.description: Hinge only: "plate" (default) gives each side one leaf along the whole length; "fingers" gives each knuckle its own finger as wide as the knuckle, the two sides' fingers alternating like two combs, so the hinge folds all the way round, and with hingeStyle "cone" and fingers as thick as the knuckle it closes flat. No leaf joins a side's fingers: join them to the model (a box and its lid). Fingers take no screw holes. "raised" lifts the second leaf so that, closed, it lies flat on the first with the clearance between, and the hinge folds well past lying flat (it prints with supports under that leaf).

gridfinityType.description: Gridfinity only: a bin, or the baseplate bins stand in, to the published Gridfinity measures so they fit parts printed from other designs, or a tray. A bin's or baseplate's size is whole grid units of 42 mm: a bin is 42 x units - 0.5 across and deep (41.5, 83.5, 125.5 ... up to 6 units, 251.5), 7 mm per height unit, up to 20 units, plus 4.4 for the stacking lip (a 3-unit bin is 25.4 tall); a baseplate is 42 x units across and deep, up to 6 units, or 12 with gridfinityLargePlate, plus its padding (gridfinityPaddingBack and the others), and 5 tall (7.4 with gridfinitySwallowtail). Any width, depth or height is rounded to the nearest whole units. When a baseplate becomes a bin, give its height too, or it gets one height unit. With gridfinityHalfGrid a bin's units are cells of 21 mm instead. A tray (#837) has no grid: a flat bottom with no feet, lip or magnet holes, its width and depth free in mm from 10 to 252 and its height from 3 to 140, kept as given within them (a new one is 80 x 40 x 20); when a baseplate becomes a tray, give its height too, or it stays 5 mm tall. The settings marked Gridfinity bin only apply to a tray too, except gridfinityLip, gridfinityLipChamfer, gridfinityMagnets and gridfinityHalfGrid; its floor starts at 1.2 mm (gridfinityFloorHeight), it takes as many compartments as leave each at least 6 mm wide (up to 24 along a side and 40 in all), its dividers and label shelves run up to its top, and its label shelves need no height units, only room, as finger scoops on any part.

gridfinityLip.description: Gridfinity bin only: the stacking lip on top of the wall that the next bin's feet sit in (default true). Switching it keeps the height units and adds or takes off the 4.4 mm.

gridfinityMagnets.description: Gridfinity bin only: holes for 6 x 2 mm magnets under each foot, 6.5 mm wide and 2.4 deep, 13 mm from the middle of the unit both ways (default false); on the half-size grid one hole under each foot, see gridfinityHalfGrid. A baseplate has none.

gridfinityHalfGrid.description: Gridfinity bin only: a half-size grid (default false). The width and depth then count cells of 21 mm: a bin is 21 x units - 0.5 (20.5, 41.5, 62.5 ... up to 12 units, 251.5), with a foot under every cell, the same steps and corners, four to a socket of an ordinary baseplate. Switching it on keeps the outline; switching it off rounds an odd count up to whole units of 42 mm. With magnets each foot gets one hole, 2.5 mm both ways from its middle towards the corner of its cell on the 42 mm grid, counted from the bin's left back corner (-x, -z). A baseplate ignores it.

gridfinityLargePlate.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: up to 12 units across and deep instead of 6 (default false), for print beds over 256 mm; a large plate of 12 x 12 is 504 mm without padding, and its exact body takes about 25 s, close to the 30 s layerling_list_edges and layerling_list_faces wait by default, so give those a larger timeoutMs. Switching it off brings a larger plate back to 6 units, its padding kept. A plate larger than the chosen printer's bed is flagged in the editor. A bin or tray ignores it.

gridfinitySwallowtail.description: Gridfinity baseplate only (#1061): Swallowtail (default false). The plate stands on a 2.4 mm floor, 7.4 mm tall, the sockets ending on it, and has half a bow-tie pocket under each side without padding, one at the middle of each cell, so two plates side by side make whole pockets across the seam. A pocket is 6 mm wide at the plate's side and 10 mm wide 7 mm in, 2 mm deep; in its bottom 0.6 mm a lip runs along its sides from 2.5 mm in, where the key's slots begin, growing to 0.2 mm at the end, and the seam itself is open. The key (gridfinityKeys) is pressed in from below, its slotted ends squeeze past the lip, and it clicks in. Not on a plate fitted to an outline (gridfinityOutline), which ignores it and stays 5 mm tall. A bin or tray ignores it.

gridfinitySwallowtailClearance.description: Gridfinity baseplate with gridfinitySwallowtail only (#1061): how much smaller than its pocket each key from gridfinityKeys is on every side, in mm (default 0.05, 0 to 0.15, to 0.01; beyond 0.15 the lip hardly holds the key). Raise it if printed keys jam or break, lower it if they sit loose. It changes only the keys laid out after it; the plate stays the same.

gridfinityLabelBack.description: Gridfinity bin only, 3 height units or more and a floor low enough (see gridfinityFloorHeight): a label shelf along the inside of the back wall (default false). The shelf is flat on top, with a 1.2 mm strip down at the front and an underside rising at 36 degrees from the wall; its top is 0.85 mm below 7 mm per height unit (20.15 mm for 3 units), so the feet of a bin stacked on the lip stay 0.5 mm clear; letters on it (gridfinityLabelBackText) take 0.4 mm of that. Shelves on several walls join at the corners; each wall has its own width, length and offset (gridfinityLabelBackWidth, gridfinityLabelBackLength, gridfinityLabelBackOffset and the same for Front, Left and Right), and the corner settings apply to all of them. A bin with compartments (gridfinityCompartmentsX/Z) does not build them and takes gridfinityCompartmentLabels instead.

gridfinityLabelFront.description: Gridfinity bin only: a label shelf along the front wall (default false), not built in a bin with compartments; see gridfinityLabelBack.

gridfinityLabelLeft.description: Gridfinity bin only: a label shelf along the left wall (default false), not built in a bin with compartments; see gridfinityLabelBack.

gridfinityLabelRight.description: Gridfinity bin only: a label shelf along the right wall (default false), not built in a bin with compartments; see gridfinityLabelBack.

gridfinityLabelBackWidth.description: Gridfinity bin only: how far the back wall's label shelf reaches out from it in mm (default 14, at least 4). The underside ends above the floor (at most about 17 in a bin of 3 height units, less with a raised floor), and across the bin the shelves and their corner pieces leave at least 2 mm open.

gridfinityLabelBackLength.description: Gridfinity bin only: the back wall's label shelf length in mm; 0 (the default), or a length that leaves at most 1 mm at both ends (1.8 mm with the stacking lip and the 0.95 mm wall), runs it from wall to wall, into the round corners. At least 10; an end that comes that close to a wall, or stops on that wall's shelf, runs into it.

gridfinityLabelBackOffset.description: Gridfinity bin only: moves the back wall's label shelf of a set length along the wall, in mm from the middle (default 0); positive is to the right (+x). It stays on its wall.

gridfinityLabelFrontWidth.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackWidth, for the front wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelFrontLength.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackLength, for the front wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelFrontOffset.description: Gridfinity bin only: moves the front wall's label shelf of a set length along the wall, in mm from the middle (default 0); positive is to the right (+x). It stays on its wall.

gridfinityLabelLeftWidth.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackWidth, for the left wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelLeftLength.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackLength, for the left wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelLeftOffset.description: Gridfinity bin only: moves the left wall's label shelf of a set length along the wall, in mm from the middle (default 0); positive is towards the front (+z). It stays on its wall.

gridfinityLabelRightWidth.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackWidth, for the right wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelRightLength.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackLength, for the right wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelRightOffset.description: Gridfinity bin only: moves the right wall's label shelf of a set length along the wall, in mm from the middle (default 0); positive is towards the front (+z). It stays on its wall.

gridfinityLabelCorner.description: Gridfinity bin only: where a label shelf meets a wall or another shelf, the corner rounded (default) or chamfered. With round, a shelf of a set length also has the front corners of its free ends rounded by the same size (at most half its width and half its length); with chamfer they stay square.

gridfinityLabelCornerSize.description: Gridfinity bin only: the size of that rounding or chamfer in mm, 0 to 10 (default 2); 0 leaves the corners sharp.

gridfinityLabelBackText.description: Gridfinity bin only, with the back wall's label shelf (gridfinityLabelBack): a text raised 0.4 mm on the shelf's top as part of the bin, one line of up to 24 characters (default none; an empty string removes it). The letters are fitted to the shelf's top, clear of the walls, the lip's support and the shelf's front, as large as it lets them or with capitals as high as gridfinityLabelTextSize; a text whose capitals would come out under 3 mm is left out. On the back and front shelves it reads from the bin's front, on the left and right ones along the wall from inside the bin. Not on a tray. Print it in another colour with a colour change at the shelf's top (20.15 mm in a bin of 3 units), which also changes the top of the walls and the lip.

gridfinityLabelFrontText.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackText, on the front wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelLeftText.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackText, on the left wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelRightText.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityLabelBackText, on the right wall's label shelf.

gridfinityLabelFont.description: Gridfinity bin only: the font of the letters on all its label shelves and compartment labels (default Multilanguage): a built-in font (Multilanguage, Sans, Serif, Script, Monospace, Rounded, Stencil, Japanese), or a font of one's own by its id (custom:...) or its name, as layerling_list_fonts gives them; any other is refused.

gridfinityLabelColor.description: Gridfinity bin only: the colour of the letters on all its label shelves and compartment labels, as #rrggbb (default none, the bin's own colour; an empty string sets it back). The bin stays one body: a 3MF gives the letters' faces, their tops and sides, this colour, which Bambu Studio reads, and then paints every face of the file with its colour's filament for OrcaSlicer, PrusaSlicer 2.9 and the slicers built on them (filaments numbered by the colours in the order they first come in the file), and an OBJ gives it to their points. STL and STEP keep one colour, and so do a group or bundle shown in one colour (multicolor false), a group cut by a hole unless multicolor is true, and a bin turned into a mesh (edge tool, hollowing, split, simplify).

gridfinityLabelTextSize.description: Gridfinity bin only: how high the capitals on all its label shelves and compartment labels are, in mm (default 0, as large as each shelf lets them). The same on every shelf, so labels of different lengths match; a shelf too small for it makes its letters as large as it lets them, and a value under 3 counts as 3.

gridfinityScoopBack.description: Gridfinity bin only, 2 height units or more and a floor low enough (see gridfinityFloorHeight): a finger scoop along the inside of the back wall (default false). The floor rises along a quarter circle into the wall, from wall to wall, so small parts can be pushed out; scoops on neighbouring walls meet in their corner, gridfinityScoopRadius applies to all of them, and a bin with a scoop has every inner floor edge rounded as much as its inner corners (2.8 mm with the 0.95 mm wall).

gridfinityScoopFront.description: Gridfinity bin only: a finger scoop along the front wall (default false); see gridfinityScoopBack.

gridfinityScoopLeft.description: Gridfinity bin only: a finger scoop along the left wall (default false); see gridfinityScoopBack.

gridfinityScoopRight.description: Gridfinity bin only: a finger scoop along the right wall (default false); see gridfinityScoopBack.

gridfinityScoopRadius.description: Gridfinity bin only: the finger scoops' radius in mm, at least 3.5. Unset, it is half the height from the floor (5.95 mm up unless gridfinityFloorHeight raises it) to where the stacking lip's support leaves the wall, 1.65 mm under 7 mm per height unit with the 0.95 mm wall (with a wall over 1.75 mm, the ledge 0.85 mm under it), or to the top of a bin without the lip: 6.7 for a bin of 3 height units with the lip, 7.525 without. It stays at least 0.5 mm less than that height, and across the bin it leaves at least 2 mm of floor, between two scoops facing each other or between a scoop and the wall opposite it.

gridfinityFloorHeight.description: Gridfinity bin only: the floor's height inside in mm, measured from the underside of the bin (default 5.95, the 1.2 mm floor on the feet). Raised, the bin is solid up to it, a blank to cut shapes into. With the lip, a bin still stacks on it up to where the stacking lip's support leaves the wall, 1.65 mm under 7 mm per height unit with the 0.95 mm wall (19.35 for 3 units), so a stacked bin's feet stay clear by 2.25 mm less the wall; with a wall over 1.75 mm, up to the ledge 0.85 mm under 7 mm per height unit. From the lip's top up, 4.4 mm over 7 mm per height unit (25.4 for 3 units), it fills the lip too: a solid block with a flat top, which no bin stacks on; a value between the two is built at the highest floor a bin still stacks on. Without the lip, at most the top of the bin, a solid block. Finger scoops start on it and label shelves can reach less far out above it; both are left out once it leaves them no room.

gridfinityOpenBack.description: Gridfinity bin only: no wall and no stacking lip along the back above the floor (default false), so bins open on facing sides stand side by side as one run. The walls beside it and their lip run straight out to the bin's outline and end square, 0.5 mm from the next bin as between any two bins, and the floor runs flat to the edge and ends square there. Feet and magnet holes stay as they are. A label shelf or finger scoop on an open side is not built, nor are the scoops against dividers facing that way (the setting is kept for when the side is closed again); shelves and scoops beside it, and dividers that meet it, run out to the edge, and a compartment takes no label on an open side. Any sides together, all four for a floor on its feet alone. A bin whose floor is raised to the top (with the lip, to the lip's top; gridfinityFloorHeight) is a solid block and has nothing to open. gridfinityOpenings opens a side only partly.

gridfinityOpenFront.description: Gridfinity bin only: no wall and no stacking lip along the front above the floor (default false), or only partly with gridfinityOpenings; see gridfinityOpenBack.

gridfinityOpenLeft.description: Gridfinity bin only: no wall and no stacking lip along the left above the floor (default false), or only partly with gridfinityOpenings; see gridfinityOpenBack.

gridfinityOpenRight.description: Gridfinity bin only: no wall and no stacking lip along the right above the floor (default false), or only partly with gridfinityOpenings; see gridfinityOpenBack.

side.description: The side switched open (gridfinityOpenBack and the others) that this entry opens.

depth.description: How deep the opening goes in mm, down from the lip's top (below its chamfer, gridfinityLipChamfer), or from the top without the lip: at least 2; unset, or within 0.5 mm of the floor, it goes down to the floor.

width.description: How wide it is along the side in mm: at least 5, at most the side's straight part between its two rounded corners; unset, or within 0.5 mm of that, it is the whole side, which runs out to the outline beside a side open in full. A side whose straight part is shorter than 5 mm is open in full.

align.description: Where a narrower opening sits along its side: start (towards -x on the back or front, towards -z on the left or right), middle (default) or end.

distance.description: With start or end: how far it is from that end of the straight part in mm (default 0), kept so the opening stays on the side.

gridfinityOpenings.description: Gridfinity bin only: how far a side switched open is opened, one entry per side. A side without an entry, or opened its whole width down to the floor, is open as without the list. Anything less keeps that side's wall, rounded corners and lip and cuts a notch with a flat bottom and square corners (unless gridfinityOpeningCorner and gridfinityOpeningCornerSize round or chamfer them) out of them: to the floor a slot, across the whole side a lower wall. The floor, the dividers and the lip beside the notch stay, so bins stack on it as on any other; a label shelf, compartment label shelf or finger scoop on that side stays off, as on any open side. A bin built solid by its wall (gridfinityWallThickness) takes no notch. An entry for a side that is not switched open is kept and does nothing, and the values are kept as given (a negative one as 0), the bin keeping the opening on its side. An empty list [] opens every switched side in full. A bin switched open on all four sides is never built solid; a side whose wall leaves no room for its opening is open in full. layerling_read_scene reports this list as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

gridfinityOutline.description: Gridfinity baseplate only (#1061): the outline it fills, as points { x, z } in mm in the plate's own frame (x across, z deep), at least three, at most 1000, enclosing one area; the plate moves to its middle and its box becomes its bounds (a width or depth given with it does not count), at most 334 mm across and deep (6 units and 41 mm a side), or 586 mm with gridfinityLargePlate, and at least 10 mm; gridfinityLargePlate stays on while the outline is wider or deeper than 334 mm. Whole 42 mm cells wholly inside it get sockets, at most 6 across and 6 deep (12 with gridfinityLargePlate), the grid moved in 2 mm steps to where it holds the most; the rest is solid; units, padding and corner radius do not apply. Width and depth then stretch the outline. An empty list takes the outline away and fits the plate to its box as a drawer. In the editor, select a baseplate and a shape to fit it into what the shape stands on (0.25 mm inside it); the outline is the plate's alone, a change of gridfinityType drops it. layerling_read_scene reports it as JSON text, stretched to the plate's box, which is accepted here as well.

gridfinityOpeningCorner.description: Gridfinity bin with a side opened partly (gridfinityOpenings) only: the corners of every notch seen from outside the wall, the two at the top where the wall's top meets the notch and the two at the bottom, rounded (default) or chamfered, by gridfinityOpeningCornerSize.

gridfinityOpeningCornerSize.description: Gridfinity bin with a side opened partly (gridfinityOpenings) only: the size of that rounding or chamfer in mm, 0 to 10 (default 0, square corners), taken to 0.01 mm; under 0.5 mm a corner stays square. The top corners take it first, up to the end of the wall's straight part and the depth, staying above the floor's rounding; the bottom ones then up to half the width and what the depth leaves. A corner that would end just beside an edge of the wall is made up to 0.5 mm smaller to keep clear of it. A notch across the whole side has no top corners.

gridfinityLipChamfer.description: Gridfinity bin with the stacking lip only: a chamfer on the lip's top edge in mm, 0 to 1 (default 0, the sharp top the specification draws). It is the edge tool's chamfer of that size, built in: that much off the outer wall and off the 45 degree slope inside, which is where the feet of a bin stacked on top rest, so a larger chamfer leaves them less to rest on. Built to 0.01 mm. The height setting and how high bins stack stay as they are; the top comes down by 0.71 x the chamfer. A bin filled to the lip's top (gridfinityFloorHeight) has no lip edge left and takes none.

gridfinityWallThickness.description: Gridfinity bin only: the wall's thickness in mm, set in from the outside, which never changes, so the bin still fits the baseplate and stacks (default 0.95, at least 0.8, at most where the walls meet). The inner corners are rounded by 3.75 mm less the wall, square from 3.75. Over 1.75 mm with the lip the wall stops at a flat ledge 0.85 mm under 7 mm per height unit, clear of a stacked bin's feet, and the floor goes no higher unless it fills the lip too (gridfinityFloorHeight); where the walls leave less than 1 mm inside, the bin is built solid. Finger scoops and label shelves are left out, and fewer compartments are built, where a thick wall leaves them no room. A bin open in full on all four sides has no wall to set and never goes solid.

gridfinityPaddingBack.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: a solid border at the plate's 5 mm height along the back, outside the grid, in mm (default 0, at most 41, to 0.01), so the plate fills a drawer that is not whole units of 42 mm. The grid stays whole units, moved away from the padded sides, and the outer corners keep their rounding (4 mm unless gridfinityCornerRadius sets it). Width and depth are the whole plate, padding included: a plate of 5 units with 19.5 mm on the right is 229.5 across. A padding given without width and depth keeps the units (on a new plate, those of the default size) and writes the size with it; a width or depth given with it is the whole plate on that axis, and the other axis keeps its units. A drawer larger than the print bed takes several baseplates, each padded on the sides that face the drawer's walls. A bin keeps the setting and ignores it.

gridfinityPaddingFront.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: the border along the front in mm (default 0, at most 41); see gridfinityPaddingBack.

gridfinityPaddingLeft.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: the border along the left in mm (default 0, at most 41); see gridfinityPaddingBack.

gridfinityPaddingRight.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: the border along the right in mm (default 0, at most 41); see gridfinityPaddingBack.

gridfinityCornerRadius.description: Gridfinity baseplate only: the radius of the plate's four outer corners in mm (default 4, as the specification draws them; 0 for square corners that sit in a drawer's corners; at most 4, to 0.01, and within 0.05 of 4 it is 4), padded or not. The sockets keep their 4 mm rounding, so bins fit as before. A bin's corners take gridfinityBinCornerRadius.

gridfinityBinCornerRadius.description: Gridfinity bin only: the radius of the bin's outer corners above its feet in mm (default 3.75, as the specification draws them; 0 for square corners, so bins side by side leave only their 0.5 mm gaps where four meet; at most 3.75, to 0.01, and within 0.05 of 3.75 it is 3.75). The feet, the inside and the lip's slopes a stacked bin rests on keep their rounding, and the wall's first 0.5 mm over the feet keeps 3.75, so the bin sits in a baseplate and stacks as before. No effect where open sides leave every corner square.

gridfinityCompartmentsX.description: Gridfinity bin only, with room above the floor (the dividers' top, 0.85 mm under 7 mm per height unit, at least 3 mm above the floor: 2 height units or more): compartments across (x), a whole number (default 1, no dividers), at most 4 per grid unit (2 per cell of the half-size grid) and at most 40 compartments in all; over that, the number across is lowered to fit. Dividers run the full height and the compartments have the bin's inner corners and a floor rounded as much (2.8 mm with the 0.95 mm wall, none from a wall of 3.75); finger scoops repeat against every divider that runs the same way as their wall, in a narrow compartment their radius is made smaller so that 2 mm of floor stays flat, and where even 3.5 mm does not fit, the scoops running that way are left out. Once a divider on an axis is moved (gridfinityDividerPositionsX/Z set), that axis keeps its positions in mm when the bin is resized; an axis left unset stays evenly spaced. Giving a count puts that axis's dividers back evenly spaced unless gridfinityDividerPositionsX/Z are given in the same call. A bin with compartments does not build the wall shelves (gridfinityLabelBack and the others); it takes gridfinityCompartmentLabels instead.

gridfinityCompartmentsZ.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityCompartmentsX, compartments deep (z).

gridfinityDividerThickness.description: Gridfinity bin only, with compartments (see gridfinityCompartmentsX): the dividers' thickness in mm, 0.8 to 3 (default 1.2).

gridfinityDividerPositionsX.description: Gridfinity bin only, with compartments across (see gridfinityCompartmentsX): each divider across, in mm from the inside of the left wall to its middle, left to right; unset they are evenly spaced. Needs one fewer value than gridfinityCompartmentsX, else they are evenly spaced; each is kept far enough from its neighbours and the walls for every compartment to stay 6 mm wide. An empty list [] puts them back evenly spaced. layerling_read_scene reports this list as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

gridfinityDividerPositionsZ.description: Gridfinity bin only: as gridfinityDividerPositionsX, each divider deep, from the inside of the back wall, back to front. An empty list [] puts them back evenly spaced.

side.description: The compartment's side the label stands against: the bin's wall or a divider.

length.description: Length in per cent of that side, 10 to 100 (default 100, the full length).

align.description: Where a shorter label sits along its side: start (towards -x on a back or front side, towards -z on a left or right side), middle (default) or end.

width.description: How far it reaches out from its side in mm (default 14, at most what leaves 6 mm open in the compartment in front of it and its corner, gridfinityLabelCornerSize).

text.description: A text raised 0.4 mm on the label, up to 24 characters, fitted as gridfinityLabelBackText is (default none).

gridfinityCompartmentLabels.description: Gridfinity bin only, with compartments (see gridfinityCompartmentsX) and 3 height units or more: a label in a compartment, with the profile and corners of the label shelves (gridfinityLabelCorner, gridfinityLabelCornerSize). One label per compartment. An empty list [] removes them all. layerling_read_scene reports this list as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

dovetailNeckWidth.description: Dovetail only: width of the narrow neck in mm; the shape's width is the wide end, its depth the length of the tail. Must be narrower than the width, by at least 0.1 mm (146 wide takes a neck of up to 145.9).

screwHoleShaft.description: Counterbore, countersink and doubleCountersink: diameter of the shaft below the head (on the doubleCountersink, between the two cones) in mm. The shape's width is the head diameter, its height the whole length; the head end of a counterbore and a countersink is on top. On a finishingWasher: the bore.

screwHoleHeadDepth.description: Counterbore and finishingWasher only. Counterbore: depth of the cylindrical head pocket in mm. FinishingWasher: depth of the seat for the screw head, from the top; the seat's top diameter is the bore plus twice this at 90 degrees.

screwHoleAngle.description: Countersink, doubleCountersink and finishingWasher: opening angle of the cone in degrees (30 to 150, default 90 for a countersunk screw). A doubleCountersink is chamfered on both faces; if it is too short for two cones they meet in the middle at this angle.

drillPointAngle.description: Cylinder set as a hole, counterbore and countersink only: a drill point at the bottom of a blind hole, the cone a drill's tip leaves, as wide as the hole (a screw hole's shaft). Its point angle in degrees, 60 to 150 (118 for a common twist drill, 135 for a split-point drill, 90 for a spot drill). As in a drawing the depth - the cylinder's height, the screw hole's length - counts to the shoulder where the cone begins; the tip reaches (diameter / 2) / tan(angle / 2) below the shape's bottom, 0.3 diameters at 118. Left out, the bottom is flat; 0 makes it flat again. A solid cylinder keeps a flat end until it is set as a hole, a doubleCountersink goes through and has none.

screwHoleSlot.description: Counterbore, countersink and doubleCountersink only: a slotted hole, for a screw that leaves the part room to be lined up before it is tightened. The head (cone or pocket) and the shaft run round the two ends of a slot and straight along its sides. The shorter of width and depth is then the head diameter and the difference the slot's length, along the longer one: width 14 and depth 6.6 make an M3 countersink slot 7.4 mm long along x. A slotted hole has no drill point. false or left out: the round hole (an oval when width and depth differ).

loftBottomOutline.description: Loft (transition) only: the outline at the bottom - round (a circle, or an ellipse when width and length differ), rectangle (corners rounded by loftBottomCorner) or polygon (loftBottomSides corners). A loft joins its bottom outline to its top outline with a straight-ruled wall: a hose adapter, a square fan onto a round duct, a stand. Its frame is what both ends need together; width and depth stretch both ends alike.

loftTopOutline.description: Loft only: the outline at the top, as loftBottomOutline.

loftBottomWidth.description: Loft only: width (x) of the bottom outline in mm.

loftBottomDepth.description: Loft only: length (z) of the bottom outline in mm.

loftTopWidth.description: Loft only: width (x) of the top outline in mm.

loftTopDepth.description: Loft only: length (z) of the top outline in mm.

loftBottomCorner.description: Loft only: corner radius of a rectangular bottom in mm (0 for sharp corners).

loftTopCorner.description: Loft only: corner radius of a rectangular top in mm.

loftBottomSides.description: Loft only: number of corners of a polygonal bottom, 3 to 24.

loftTopSides.description: Loft only: number of corners of a polygonal top, 3 to 24.

loftOffsetX.description: Loft only: how far the top's middle sits from the bottom's along the width (x), in mm; the bottom stays in place when it changes.

loftOffsetZ.description: Loft only: how far the top's middle sits from the bottom's along the length (z), in mm.

loftWall.description: Loft only: wall thickness in mm. 0 (default) is a solid body; more makes a tube open at both ends, the opening inset by the wall at the bottom and at the top.

loftSegments.description: Loft only: 16 to 360 (default 96), how many straight pieces a full circle or rounded corner is drawn with in the view and in STL, OBJ and 3MF. More pieces look rounder and make larger files.

loftSmooth.description: Loft only: 0 to 1 (default 0), how much of an S-curve the sides take between the two ends instead of a straight line: the sides leave both ends straight up and change their size in between, like a hose adapter that flares smoothly from a narrow to a wide pipe. It works with a wall, a twist, a tilt and an offset.

loftTwist.description: Loft only: degrees the section turns from bottom to top about the vertical, evenly on the way up, -360 to 360 (default 0). The sides then wind round.

loftTiltX.description: Loft only: degrees the top end tilts about the x axis, -45 to 45: positive raises its front (+z) edge. The sections tilt evenly on the way up; the highest point stays at the height, and a tilt too steep for the height is reduced.

loftTiltZ.description: Loft only: degrees the top end tilts about the z axis, -45 to 45: positive raises its right (+x) side. Same as loftTiltX otherwise.

at.description: Where the section stands, as a share of the height from the bottom, 0.01 to 0.99.

outline.description: Its outline: circle or ellipse, rectangle with corner, regular polygon.

width.description: Its width in mm, at least 1.

depth.description: Its length in mm, at least 1.

corner.description: Rectangle only: corner radius in mm.

sides.description: Polygon only: number of corners, 3 to 24.

offsetX.description: How far its middle sits from the bottom's middle across the width, in mm.

offsetZ.description: How far its middle sits from the bottom's middle along the length, in mm.

loftSections.description: Loft only (#1034): sections between the bottom and the top, sorted up the height, at most 12; the body goes through all of them (loftThrough). Twist, tilt and loftSmooth apply to a loft between two ends only and are left aside while there are sections. An empty list [] removes them. layerling_read_scene reports this list as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

loftThrough.description: Loft only, with loftSections: smooth (default) is one curved surface through every section, straight flat walls from section to section.

slotEndRatio.description: Capsule (slot) only: the small end's diameter as a share of the large one, 0.1 to 1 (default 1, two equal ends). The large end sits at the start of the long axis, the small one at its end, the sides run as tangents to both - a belt guard. The large diameter is the capsule's short side; the centre distance is the long side less both radii.

torusTubeRatio.description: Torus only: how thick the tube is seen from above, as a share of the torus's outer size, 0.01 to 0.5 (0.5 closes the hole). The height only squashes or stretches the tube, so a flat ring keeps its hole; resizing the torus scales the tube along. A tube as thick as the torus is high keeps the torus an exact CAD body.

dovetailClearance.description: Dovetail only: gap in mm (0 to 2, default 0.2, or the printer's play when one is set with layerling_printer_play) added on every side while the dovetail is a hole - a copy of the tail set to hole cuts a socket the tail fits into.

portProfile.description: Port opening only: rounded corners (default), or the lower corners cut off at a slant as on an HDMI, Mini HDMI, Micro HDMI or Mini DisplayPort socket, or only the lower left one as on DisplayPort; xt60 and xt30 a lying outline with one end narrowed by two cut corners, mt60 a rounded triangle, dsub9 the D-Sub's trapezoid - these four have every corner rounded by cornerFillet. The cut grows with width and height.

portClearance.description: Port opening only: extra room in mm (0 to 2, default 0) on every side, on top of the room a portPreset has already. Together with portPreset when creating, it makes the opening wider and taller by twice this and its corners rounder by it. On its own it does not change the size; it records the extra room, so the inspector still shows the preset.

cornerFillet.description: Rounded box and port opening only. Rounded box: fillet radius of vertical corners in mm. Port opening: radius of the opening's four corners in mm, at most half its width or height (half the height gives fully round ends, as on USB-C).

topBottomFillet.description: Rounded box only: fillet radius of top and bottom edges in mm (the top edge only, when bottomFillet is given).

bottomFillet.description: Rounded box only: fillet radius of the bottom edge in mm, on its own; left out, the bottom takes topBottomFillet. Top and bottom together cannot exceed the height.

roundedBoxQuality.description: Rounded box only: quality / segment count for fillet rounding (1 to 32; 1 gives chamfered corners).

bentTubeInnerProfile.description: Bent tube only: inner cross-section; "none" makes a solid tube.

bentTubeSize.description: Bent tube only: outer diameter of a round tube, width across flats of a polygonal one, in mm (1 to 500).

bentTubeWall.description: Bent tube only: wall thickness in mm. With different inner and outer profiles it is the thinnest point of the wall.

bentTubeQuality.description: Bent tube only: sides of a round profile and fineness of the bends (12 to 96).

length.description: Straight run before the bend, in mm (0 to 1000).

bendAngle.description: Bend after the straight run, in degrees (-180 to 180); 0 means no bend.

bendRadius.description: Centre-line radius of the bend in mm; at least half the outer size (corner distance for polygons) plus 0.1.

roll.description: Turns the plane of this bend about the running direction, relative to the previous bend, in degrees.

bentTubeSegments.description: Bent tube only: the chain of segments, each a straight run followed by an arc bend. The tube starts along +X; roll 0 bends within the workplane, roll 90 bends upward. layerling_read_scene reports this list as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

vase.description: Vase only: its settings, by the vase tool's own (German) names, for example { profile: "bauchig" (or flasche, schale, fass, zylinder, trichter), section: "vieleck" (or kreis, welle), polySides: 6, sectionWaves: 12, sectionWaveStyle: "weich" (or spitz, bogen, lamellen), twist: 90, swayAngle: 10, body: "voll" (one wall for the slicer's vase mode) or "hohl" with wall and bottom in mm (bottom 0: no bottom, a tube open at both ends, for bells and mouthpieces), effect: "rillen" (or keine, streifen, voronoi, lowpoly), ribCount: 48, ribDepth: 1.6, stripeCount, voronoiCell, lowpolyAround, zoneFrom/zoneTo in % of the height, quality: "entwurf", "standard" or "fein" }. Also: section2 (a second cross-section the first blends into, between section2From and section2To %), waveAmplitude/waveCount (winding grooves), and bottom and wall: watertight: "ja", drainHoles, drainDiameter, floorSlope, footHeight, rubberFeet, cutout (keine, voronoi, waben, rauten, kreise; cutoutSize, cutoutWeb, cutoutFrom, cutoutTo) and lamp (keine, haengend, stehend, puck; lampSocket e27, e14 or eigen with lampHole) for a hollow vase, reinforce (keine, rippen, doppelwand; reinforceCount, reinforceDepth) for a solid one. Drawn shapes: profile "gezeichnet" with profilePoints [[height 0..1, radius 0..1, kind?, slope?], ...] (kind 1 a corner, 2 a handle with its slope; the widest point is the diameter), section or section2 "gezeichnet" with drawSymmetry (halb, viertel, windmuehle with drawRepeat blades, frei) and drawPoints [{ x, y, corner, tx?, ty? }, ...] in the unit circle (the part the symmetry repeats), twistMode "kurve" with twistPoints [[height 0..1, angle in degrees, kind?, slope?], ...]. Accessories: legMode (keine, stecken = legs to plug in, angeformt = moulded on, staender = a stand; legCount, legHeight, legDiameter, legShape kegel/zylinder/kantig, legSplay, legInset), saucerMode (keine, schale = a saucer, versteckt = hidden in the foot; saucerHeight, saucerGap, saucerWall, saucerRibs/saucerSpout/saucerGrip "ja" or "nein"), insertMode (keine, pflanze, bewaesserung, stecker, roehrchen; insertWall, insertStandoff, reservoirHeight, frogHole, tubeDiameter) for a hollow vase, lidMode (keiner, stuelp, schnapp, schraube, kanne = a teapot lid: the top lidHeight mm of a hollow vase is the lid, its pattern and twist running on, a lip into the opening, lidKnob "ja" a knob apart; lidClearance, lidThickness, lidDepth, threadPitch, lidGrip) and fitClearance; vaseParts lays them out as objects. For printing: material (pla, petg, abs, asa, tpu) and lineWidth (the slicer's line in vase mode, mm), which the editor's Print card weighs. Settings not given stay as they were (when creating: the vase tool's defaults). The height is the object's height and the widest diameter its larger side; the other side follows the outline. layerling_read_scene reports the settings that differ from the defaults as JSON text, which is accepted here as well.

font.description: Text only: a built-in font (Multilanguage, Sans, Serif, Script, Monospace, Rounded, Stencil), or a font of one's own by its id (custom:...) or its name, as layerling_list_fonts gives them.

textCurved.description: Text only: true bends the line along a circle. Width and depth then follow radius and letter size.

textRadius.description: Curved text only: radius of the circle the baseline follows, in mm (5 to 500).

textSize.description: Curved text only: letter size in mm. Defaults to the size the straight text had.

textInward.description: Curved text only: true runs the line along the bottom of the circle, letters pointing at the centre.

textFlipped.description: Curved text only: true keeps the line where it is on the circle but turns the letters upside down, to be read from the other side.

vaseParts.description: Vase only: true also lays out the vase's accessories (legs to plug in, a stand, a saucer, an insert, a lid, as its settings ask for) as objects of their own beside it, ready to print; the ones laid out for this vase before are replaced. Returns them as parts; accessories this vase does not allow (an insert through a narrow neck) are listed as notPossible.

gridfinityKeys.description: Gridfinity baseplate with gridfinitySwallowtail only (#1061): true also lays out the plate's keys in front of it, flat on its level, as sketch bodies ready to print: one for each pocket at its back and right, so that every pocket across a seam with the next plate gets one. Each key is 1.4 mm thick, the pocket less gridfinitySwallowtailClearance on every side (14 x 10 mm less twice that), with a slot of 1.2 x 4.5 mm into each end. Returns them as parts; a second call lays them out again, and the keys laid out for the plate before are removed. Unless the object is a baseplate with gridfinitySwallowtail and pockets at its back or right (sides without padding), the call fails before changing anything; keys that cannot be made after that come back in notPossible with the reason.

threadSize.description: Thread only: a standard size by name, as the editor's size menu lists it. Sets threadDiameter and threadPitch; if those come along (as in a settings block read back), they must match the size. A G size is a Whitworth pipe thread (BSPP, ISO 228-1, for fittings, water, gas, hydraulics and pneumatics): G1/2 is 20.955 mm with 14 threads per inch. It switches a v profile to whitworth, and an M, UNC or UNF size switches whitworth back to v; trapezoidal and round stay, and a threadProfile in the same call wins. PCO 1881 is the 28 mm neck of most water and soda bottles (27.4 mm, pitch 2.7): it sets the custom profile with threadDepth 1.6 and threadFlankAngle 30 unless the call gives them; the neck is a rod, the cap a nut or bore. S60x6 (IBC) is the outlet thread of IBC containers (DIN 6063-1, KS 60: 60 mm, pitch 6, core 54): it sets the custom profile with threadDepth 3 and threadFlankAngle 30 the same way. An NPT size (1/16" NPT to 4" NPT, ASME B1.20.1) is the American tapered pipe thread: the pipe's outside diameter (1/2" NPT is 21.336 mm with 14 threads per inch), the custom profile with 60-degree flanks and 0.779 pitch deep, and threadTaper true; another size makes a tapered thread straight again, unless the call gives threadTaper.

align_objects.description: Align two or more Layerling objects using the same alignment logic as the editor Alignment button. On the plate the axes are the world's; with a workplane set on a face (layerling_set_workplane) the objects are measured and moved along that plane's axes instead - x along the face, y out of it, z across - so a part turned 45° lines up with its own edges. mode size is the editor's Alt on an align dot: the objects stay where they are and change their size instead - min or max stretches each one, its other side fixed, to that side of the anchor (or of the farthest object without one); center gives each one the anchor's size along the axis (or the largest object's), its middle fixed. An object turned at some other angle than square to the axis is left as it is and counted in skipped. mode spread is the editor's equal-gaps dot (target is not needed): three or more objects are spread along the axis so the space between neighbouring edges is the same; the first and last stay. An object that runs past all the others along the axis and is longer than each (a board, a tray) is found by itself as a frame: the others spread inside it with the same gap at its edges, a single one comes to its middle.
