Objects in several rows (boxes overlapping across the axis, on both other axes) spread row by row; where they stand in no clean rows, objects side by side that overlap along the axis move together as one block (a whole row of a puzzle tray, front to back). gap (mm) lines them up that far apart instead, from the anchor or a locked object or else the first; in a frame the row is centred. Locked objects and the anchor never move; problem says tooFew, noRoom or lockedBetween when nothing could move, gaps the gap each row got.

ids.description: Object ids to align. If omitted, uses the current selection.

anchorId.description: Optional object id to keep fixed as the alignment reference, or "plate": the build plate is the reference - the objects line up on its edges or middle, and mode spread spreads them over the whole plate with the same gap to its edges.

axis.description: x=left/right, z=front/back, y=bottom/top - or along the set workplane's x, z and normal.

target.description: Which side/center to align. Required for position and size.

mode.description: position (default) moves the objects; size stretches them to the reference instead; spread gives them equal gaps along the axis.

gap.description: Only with mode spread: the gap between the objects in mm, instead of spreading them evenly.

scale_objects.description: Scale objects by a percentage, the same in every direction - the editor's Scale by percent tool. 120 makes them a fifth larger, 50 half the size. mode together (default) scales them around their common centre, so the layout grows with them; each scales every object where it stands, so the gaps stay. The bottom stays where it is. Locked objects are left as they are. One undo step.

ids.description: Object ids to scale. If omitted, uses the current selection.

percent.description: The new size in percent of the current one.

mode.description: together (default): around the common centre. each: every object in place.

lay_flat.description: Turn objects so one of their faces rests on the workplane - the editor's Lay flat on face tool. Name a side of the object's own box (face) or give the outward normal of the face in world coordinates (normal); either snaps to the nearest real face. Several objects turn together about their common centre and keep their spacing. One undo step.

ids.description: Object ids to lay flat. If omitted, uses the current selection.

face.description: Side of the object's own box that should end up on the plate, taken in the object's current turn.

normal.description: Outward normal [x, y, z] of the face to put down, in world coordinates (y is up). Wins over face.

referenceId.description: With several ids: whose face is meant. Defaults to the first id.

place_on_face.description: Set objects down on a face of another object, as the editor's C key (Tinkercad's Cruise) does: their underside - the bottom of the first object as it stands - turns onto the face, sloped faces included, lined up with it the way a new shape dropped there would be (keeping its own turn about its up axis), and the middle of that underside lands on the point. Name the target object and its face as a side of its own box (snaps to the nearest real face; the point is then the middle of the target brought straight onto that face), or give point and normal yourself. Several objects move together and keep their spacing. One undo step.

ids.description: Object ids to set down. If omitted, uses the current selection.

targetId.description: The object whose face they go on.

targetFace.description: Side of the target's own box, taken in its current turn (default top).

point.description: Where the underside's middle lands, [x, y, z] in world coordinates (y up). With normal, wins over targetId.

normal.description: Outward normal [x, y, z] of the face at point, in world coordinates.

mate_faces.description: Move one object so a face of it meets a face of another object - the editor's Align faces tool. The moving object is turned the shortest way until the faces are parallel (not at all if they already are), then slid along the target face's normal only, so it keeps its place sideways. mode against puts the faces face to face (touching, back to back), flush lays them in one plane side by side. gap leaves that much room, measured out of the target face. Faces are named as sides of each object's own box and snap to the nearest real face. mode concentric instead puts a round face of the object (the inside of a hole, the outside of a pin) on the axis of a round face of the target - a hole over a hole, a pin into a hole: give facePoint and targetFacePoint, a point on or near each round face (a point on the hole's axis works too); the object turns the shortest way until the axes are parallel, then slides across onto the target axis and keeps its depth along it. mode point moves the object straight, without turning it, so point (a corner, a spot on an edge, a reference point) lands on targetPoint; targetId is not needed, and axes limits the move: ["x", "z"] puts the point straight above or below the target point, ["elevation"] brings it to the same height. Up to two more pairs then turn it, like aligning by three points: point2 and targetPoint2 turn it about the first point until the line through point2 runs through targetPoint2; point3 and targetPoint3 then turn it about the line from the first target point to targetPoint2 until point3 lies in the plane through that line and targetPoint3. Give point2 and point3 where they are now, before the move. One undo step.

face.description: Its face that should meet the other, as a side of its own box. Needed unless mode is concentric.

targetId.description: The object that stays where it is. Needed unless mode is point.

targetFace.description: The face of the target to meet. Needed unless mode is concentric.

mode.description: against (default): face to face. flush: in one plane, side by side. concentric: two round faces on one axis (needs facePoint and targetFacePoint instead of face and targetFace). point: a point of the object onto another point (needs point and targetPoint).

facePoint.description: concentric only: a point on or near the object's round face, in the numbers layerling_read_scene reports.

targetFacePoint.description: concentric only: a point on or near the target's round face.

gap.description: Room between the planes in millimetres, measured out of the target face. Default 0.

point.description: point only: the spot on the object that should land on targetPoint, for example a corner from layerling_list_edges or a reference point.

targetPoint.description: point only: where that spot should land, for example a corner of another object or a reference point from layerling_list_reference_points.

axes.description: point only: the axes the object moves along. Default all three.

point2.description: point only, optional: a second spot on the object, where it is now. The object turns about the first point until the line through this spot runs through targetPoint2.

targetPoint2.description: point only: the point the line from the first point through point2 should run through.

point3.description: point only, optional, after point2: a third spot on the object, where it is now. The object turns about the line the first two pairs fixed until this spot lies in the plane through that line and targetPoint3.

targetPoint3.description: point only: the point that fixes that plane, on the same side of the line.

open_group.description: Open a group to change its parts one by one, like 'Edit group' in the editor: the parts lie loose on the workplane (their ids come back) and can be changed with every other tool. Close it again with layerling_close_group. While a group is open, a group among its parts can be opened too, one level deeper each time; any other group is refused until the open one is closed. layerling_read_scene reports the innermost open group as openGroup and every level, outermost first, as openGroups.

id.description: The group to open: any group when none is open, otherwise one of the innermost open group's parts. If omitted, the one selected object.

close_group.description: Close the innermost open group: rebuild it from its parts (the editor's Done) as the same group, keeping its id, name, colour and solid/hole state; or pass cancel: true to put the untouched group back. The level around it, if any, stays open. Fillets and chamfers applied to the whole group are lost on rebuild.

cancel.description: true puts the group back unchanged instead of rebuilding it.

group_objects.description: Group objects by id using Layerling's normal grouping/boolean pipeline.

intersect_objects.description: Keep only what the given objects have in common, like the editor's Intersection button. Pass two or more solids (each counts as it looks, a group with its holes) or solids and holes (all solids against all holes). The result replaces the operands and can be opened like a group; no overlap leaves nothing and reports empty.

ungroup_objects.description: Ungroup one or more grouped objects by id and preserve their edited geometry.

boolean_cut.description: Cut solids with hole objects. Provide solidIds and holeIds; the result replaces the operands.

separate_parts.description: Separate one disconnected multi-part object into independent objects. An extruded sketch body comes apart by its outlines instead: one exact body per outer outline (with the holes inside it), overlapping outlines included, each keeping its own sketch.

wrap_around_cylinder.description: Wrap one body that lies flat on the plate around a cylinder about the vertical, as the editor's "Wrap around a cylinder" does - an imported SVG, text or any other body. Seen from above, left to right runs around the cylinder, the back edge becomes the top, and the thickness stands out of the wall (inward: true puts it into the wall, for an engraving with a hole). The result is one mesh body whose middle is the cylinder's axis: centre it on the cylinder with layerling_align_objects (x and z centre) and it sits on that wall. One undo step brings the flat body back; to try another diameter, undo first. Fails when the body is longer than the circumference. Returns the new object.

id.description: The body to wrap; defaults to the one selected body.

diameter.description: Diameter of the cylinder wall in mm, for example the outside of a cup.

inward.description: Put the thickness into the wall instead of out of it. Default false.

simplify_mesh.description: Reduce the triangle count of one imported mesh (decimation), as the editor's "Simplify mesh" does - for a dense STL, OBJ, 3MF or STEP import, or the mesh a cut, merge or wrap left behind. Use it when a mesh is too complex to cut (the cut reports the triangle count and the limit) or makes the editor slow. Pass either keepPercent or targetTriangles. Fine detail goes first; the body keeps its size and position, and the simplifier stops early rather than close holes or merge walls, so the count reached can stay above a very low target. Sharp edges (faces meeting at more than 30 degrees) and the rims of holes stay exactly where they are, as the panel's "Keep edges and holes" does: flat faces lose most of their triangles, a bore stays as round as it was; pass keepEdges false to let them be rounded off for a lower count. The result is one plain mesh body: a group simplified this way can no longer be ungrouped or opened. One undo step brings the old mesh back. Shapes from the catalogue have no mesh to simplify; lower their sides or quality instead. Returns the object with trianglesBefore, trianglesAfter and keepEdges.

id.description: The mesh to simplify; defaults to the one selected body.

keepPercent.description: Share of the triangles to keep, above 0 and below 100. 50 halves the count.

targetTriangles.description: Number of triangles to aim for, below the current count (importedTriangles in layerling_list_objects).

keepEdges.description: Keep sharp edges and the rims of holes exactly. Default true.

save_custom_shape.description: Keep bodies as a custom shape, as the shape library's "Save selection" does, to insert them into any design later. Several bodies become one shape and come back together. The shape is kept centred, standing on the plate. Where the shared server store is on, it goes to the server's "Custom shapes" folder unless location says "browser"; otherwise it stays in this browser. Returns the new shape's id, name, location and folder.

ids.description: The bodies to keep; defaults to the selection.

name.description: Name shown in the library; defaults to the body's name. On the server it is also the file name, so it must not be taken yet.

location.description: Where to keep it. Default: the server when there is one, else the browser.

folder.description: Folder path to put it in, on that side (browser or server), with / between levels, e.g. "Brackets/M3"; at most three levels. Missing folders on the way are made. Default: no folder, the top of the list.

list_custom_shapes.description: List the custom shapes: those on the server (ids start with "server:") and those in this browser, with name, location, folder path ("Brackets/M3", null for none) and size, plus the folder paths on each side (folders go three levels deep). serverAvailable says whether this installation has the shared store.

insert_custom_shape.description: Insert a custom shape into the open design, as a click on its tile does. Without x/z it lands at the workplane's origin; with them, the middle of its footprint goes there and it stands on the plate. Returns the inserted objects, which are selected.

id.description: Id from layerling_list_custom_shapes, or the shape's name.

name.description: The shape's name, instead of the id.

x.description: Where the middle goes, in mm.

z.description: Where the middle goes, in mm.

delete_custom_shape.description: Remove a custom shape from the browser or the server. Bodies already inserted into designs stay. Cannot be undone.

id.description: Id from layerling_list_custom_shapes, or the shape's name.

name.description: The shape's name, instead of the id.

split_objects.description: Cut solids or holes in two with a plane, like the editor's Split tool. Each object the plane crosses is replaced by two closed mesh bodies - two holes for a hole - and a hollowed body keeps its cavity; named with the side they lie on, e.g. "Box (Z+)" and "Box (Z-)"; objects the plane misses stay as they are. Axes as in a slicer: `axis` x cuts across left-right, y across front-back, z horizontally (default). `position` is where the plane crosses, in millimetres, in the numbers layerling_read_scene reports: position.x for x, position.z for y, elevation for z; it defaults to the middle and must lie inside the objects. `rotationX`, `rotationY` and `rotationZ` tilt the plane in degrees (-180 to 180, default 0) for an angled cut, about the two axes it does not cut across: an x cut turns about y and z, a y cut about z and x, a z cut about x and y; the angle about the cut axis itself is refused. With both set, the plane turns about the first of the pair (y for x, z for y, x for z) and then about the other. With a tilt, `position` is measured along the tilted plane's normal. `connectors` lines the halves up again, like the panel's Connectors: "dowels" drills a hole into each half and adds the loose pins as a third body standing beside them, named e.g. "Box (dowels)"; "plugs" stands round pegs on the minus half that go into holes in the plus half; "dovetail" stands a tongue that widens away from the cut face on the minus half, running straight across it from edge to edge, and cuts the matching groove right through the plus half, so the halves slide together sideways along it and then cannot pull apart; "none" (default) splits as before. Dowels and plugs go perpendicular to the plane, the middle of each at least its diameter plus 1.2 mm from every edge of the cut face; each separate piece of the cut face gets `connectorCount` (0 = as many as its size suits, at least two), fewer where there is less room, none where there is no room, and none where a half is thinner than the hole. A dovetail's tongues lie side by side, `connectorCount` per piece (0 = one for every six tongue widths across it, at least one), each with half its top width, half its width and 1.2 mm to the edges beside it; they run along the long way of the cut face, turned by `dovetailDirection`, all pieces of one body the same way. Holes are split without. The result returns the angles used, the new objects, the ids that were split, the plane's range (`min`, `max`) and, with connectors, what they came to (`connectors`: the settings used, `placed`, `faces`, `tooSmall` pieces, `tooThin` left out). One undo step; the parts lose their editable shape settings.

ids.description: Solids or holes to split; the current selection when omitted.

axis.description: Direction the plane cuts across (z is up), default z.

position.description: Where the plane crosses in millimetres; the middle when omitted.

rotationX.description: Tilt about the left-right axis in degrees, -180 to 180, default 0. Not for an x cut.

rotationY.description: Tilt about the front-back axis in degrees, -180 to 180, default 0. Not for a y cut.

rotationZ.description: Tilt about the vertical axis in degrees, -180 to 180, default 0. Not for a z cut.

alongWorkplane.description: Lay the plane on the current workplane (parallel) or square to it across its X or Y direction, like the panel's "Align to workplane"; sets axis and tilt itself, so leave those out. Without position the plane goes through the workplane's origin when that crosses the objects, otherwise through their middle.

connectors.description: Connectors through the cut face that line the halves up again: dowels (holes in both halves and loose pins beside them), plugs (pegs on the minus half, holes in the plus half) or dovetail (a widening tongue across the minus half's cut face, its groove through the plus half; slide the halves together along it). Default none.

connectorCount.description: Connectors on each separate piece of the cut face, 0 to 16 - for a dovetail the tongues side by side; 0 (default) as many as its size suits. Only with connectors.

connectorDiameter.description: Diameter of the pins or pegs in mm, 2 to 20, default 5. Only with dowels or plugs.

connectorDepth.description: How deep each hole goes into its half in mm, 2 to 30, default 6; a dowel is twice that less 0.6 mm long, a peg stands that less 0.3 mm. Only with dowels or plugs.

dowelBase.description: Only with dowels: true stands the loose dowels on a breakaway base, a 1.3 mm plate that holds on to the bed with a socket round each dowel's foot and a small nub it stands on, raised 0.5 mm - for a printer whose bed moves, where standing dowels wobble loose. Default false.

connectorClearance.description: Room per side between a pin, peg or tongue and its hole or groove in mm, 0 to 0.5; default the printer's play when one is set, otherwise 0.2. Only with connectors.

dovetailWidth.description: The dovetail tongue's width where it leaves the cut face in mm, 3 to 30, default 6; it widens from there by its flanks. Only with connectors dovetail.

dovetailDepth.description: How far the tongue stands out of the cut face into the other half in mm, 1.5 to 15, default 4; the groove is 0.3 mm deeper. Only with connectors dovetail.

dovetailAngle.description: How far each flank of the tongue leans out from square to the cut face, in degrees, 5 to 30, default 15. Only with connectors dovetail.

dovetailDirection.description: Which way the tongues run, in degrees from the long way of the cut face, -90 to 90: 0 (default) along it, 90 across it. Only with connectors dovetail.

list_edges.description: List real CAD edge ids for one object so a later chamfer/fillet can target specific edges.

hollow_object.description: Hollow a solid into walls of equal thickness, like a box, cup or case. A hole can be hollowed too and stays a hole. The walls grow inward, so the outside keeps its size. `openings` chooses which flat sides stay open, measured against the world's axes: a list of any of top, bottom, front (+z), back (-z), left (-x) and right (+x) - for example ["front"] for a drawer slot - or one of the names top (default), bottom, top-bottom, or none for a sealed cavity. A side asked for in a list must have a flat face at the very edge of the body on that side. `edges` sets how the inner walls meet where the body has a step or opening: round (default, radius = wall thickness) or sharp. Can be undone like an edge treatment. Resizing the body later hollows it again at the new size a moment afterwards, so the walls keep their thickness.

array_objects.description: Repeat objects n times in a row, in a grid or around a circle - hole rows, hole grids, bolt circles, the teeth of a ring - like the editor's Pattern tool. `count` includes the originals. Coordinates are as in a slicer: X to the right, Y to the back, Z up. A row steps `spacing` millimetres along `direction` (negative runs the other way), or along several axes at once with `spacingX`, `spacingY` and `spacingZ` (a diagonal row, a staircase; give any of them and the others count as 0). A grid lays `count` columns along X, `spacingX` apart, and `rows` rows along Y, `spacingY` apart (negative runs to the left or the front; left out, the pieces' size plus 5 mm). Each can be 1, for a single line along Y or X; columns times rows is at most 100, past that the rows are cut back. The answer's `grid` gives the columns and rows made, with `capped: true` when the rows were cut. With `fitAxis` a row is spread evenly over a body instead - holes along a plate: the last piece ends as far from the body's far end as the original stands from its nearer one, and `edgeGap` sets that gap first. A circle turns about the vertical axis through (`centerX`, `centerY`) over `angle` degrees: 360 (default) spreads the pieces evenly, a smaller angle puts the first and last piece on its ends; positive runs counter-clockwise seen from above. `rise` lifts every copy that many millimetres more than the one before (a screw, an ascending spiral) and `radiusChange` moves it that far further from the centre (negative: closer) for a flat or conical spiral. `rotateCopies` (default true) turns each copy with the circle. The copies are added as one undo step and returned with their ids; the originals stay where they are, unless `edgeGap` moves them. A circle leaves its centre as the pieces' pivot (their selection's, or the group's with `group: true`), halfway up the pieces, and returns it as `pivot` (X, Y, Z), so another part can be aligned to the true centre rather than the middle of the pieces' box.

ids.description: Objects to repeat; the current selection when omitted.

count.description: Pieces including the originals, 2 to 100. Grid: the columns along X, 1 to 100.

rows.description: Grid: rows along Y including the originals' row, 1 to 100, default 1.

direction.description: Row: axis to step along (z is up). Used with `spacing`.

spacingX.description: Row: step along X in millimetres per copy. With spacingY / spacingZ the row runs along several axes at once. Grid: from column to column.

spacingY.description: Row: step along Y (towards the back) in millimetres per copy. Grid: from row to row.

spacingZ.description: Row: step along Z (up) in millimetres per copy.

angle.description: Circle: total angle in degrees, default 360.

centerX.description: Circle: centre X in millimetres, default 0.

centerY.description: Circle: centre Y in millimetres (towards the back), default 0.

rotateCopies.description: Circle: turn the copies with the circle, default true.

rise.description: Circle: height gained per copy in millimetres, default 0 (a screw when not 0).

radiusChange.description: Circle: distance from the centre gained per copy in millimetres, default 0 (a spiral when not 0; negative tightens).

fitAxis.description: Row: spread the row evenly over a body along X or Y, like a row of holes in a plate. The last piece keeps the same gap to the body's far end as the original has to its nearer end, and the spacing follows `count` (spacing and direction are then ignored).

fitTo.description: Row with fitAxis: id of the body to spread over; left out, the smallest body whose footprint holds the middle of the pieces.

edgeGap.description: Row with fitAxis: first move the originals so they stand this many millimetres in from the body's nearer end (from the edge to the piece's side, not its centre).

group.description: Group the originals and the copies into one object in the same step, as Group does (holes among them cut the solids), default false. If grouping fails the pieces stay loose and `warning` says why.

apply_edge_treatment.description: Apply chamfer, chamfillet or fillet to specific edge ids returned by layerling_list_edges, on a solid or a hole (a hole stays a hole: a box hole with filleted vertical edges cuts a pocket with round inside corners), to "all" sharp edges, to the "top" edges (every edge along the body's highest level, such as the rim of a cookie cutter), to the "bottom" edges (every edge along its lowest level, such as the foot of a part), or to the "vertical" edges (every edge that stands straight up, such as the corners of a box), as the editor's Top edges, Bottom edges and Vertical edges buttons pick them. A chamfillet is the printable foot: a chamfer at the plate (chamferAngle 15 to 75, default 45) that blends tangentially into a fillet toward the wall, so the foot needs no support and ends soft; amount is the height it takes up, and it is mostly used with "bottom". A fillet with endAmount has a variable radius: it runs from amount at one end of the edge to endAmount at the other, on exactly one edge id; if the large end comes out where the small one should be, apply it again with the two values swapped. A fillet with concave true is the negative of a rounding: it scoops a quarter-round out of each straight edge (a cylinder of radius amount lying on the edge), as a notch in the corners of a box, instead of rounding the edge off. When the kernel refuses a chamfer or plain fillet, layerling tries once more with the short edges (up to twice the size) at the ends of the picked ones, as where an earlier chamfer ends on a wall still sharp; the ones it took along come back as cornerEdgeIds and are part of selectedEdgeIds.

endAmount.description: Fillet of one edge only: the radius at the edge's other end, for a radius that changes along it (#687).

concave.description: Fillet only: scoop the straight edges out (a cylinder of radius amount on each edge) instead of rounding them (#1160).

inspect_errors.description: Inspect the editor notice, last MCP error and active edge modifier error, plus the last messages and errors of this session (recentNotices, recentErrors, with times) - the same lists the editor's bug report carries.

bundle_objects.description: Bundle objects like Tinkercad's Ctrl+B: they move, turn and scale together as one object, but nothing is merged - every part keeps its colour and its solid or hole setting, holes cut nothing, and in an STL, 3MF or OBJ export every part is a body of its own (so a two-colour logo on a plate stays two coloured parts). A bundle is not one body: the edge tools and hollowing refuse it. layerling_ungroup_objects takes it apart again, layerling_open_group opens it for editing. Grouped with other objects later (layerling_group_objects), a bundle's holes cut those objects but never the bundle's own solids, as in Tinkercad; to let a hole cut its own bundle, ungroup it and group its parts. Use layerling_group_objects instead when the parts should become one body.

ids.description: At least two objects to bundle.

measure_section.description: Measure on a cut through the design, like "Measure" in the editor's section view: wall thickness, a gap, a clearance. Without axis and offset it measures on the section view as it is set, also when it is turned to the workplane or the view; the points are then given and returned in world coordinates and land on that plane. Both points snap to the outline of the cut (within snapRadius mm, default 1): first to the nearest wall, then the second one preferably square to its wall as seen from the first - give it a point near the opposite wall and it returns the true thickness. Points are in the editor's coordinates (x, z, elevation); the one along the axis is set to the plane. axis and offset work like layerling_export_section_svg and default to the section view or the middle of the design. Round outlines (a hole, a cylinder) also snap: the centre of the circle; a second point near the spot across the centre from a first one on the circle lands exactly across, so the distance is the diameter; and with the centre as the first point the second lands on the circle, so the distance is the radius. Returns the snapped points with their snap kind (perpendicular, corner, outline, center, opposite or free), distance, circle ("diameter", "radius" or null) and deltaX, deltaZ, deltaElevation. The section view itself is left as it is.

offset.description: Where the plane cuts, in mm.

from.description: First point near a wall: { x, z, elevation }.

to.description: Second point near the other wall: { x, z, elevation }.

snapRadius.description: How far a point may be from the outline to snap, mm (default 1).

show_overhangs.description: Find overhangs that would need supports, like "Show overhangs" in the editor's visibility menu: faces that lean towards the plate more steeply than angle (degrees from vertical; a wall is 0, a flat ceiling 90). enabled switches the red tint in the view on or off; angle (30-70, default 45) is kept in the design's settings. Faces lying on the plate do not count. Returns enabled, angle and, for each visible solid (or the given ids), overhangAreaMm2, lowestOverhangHeight and steepestOverhangAngle (the steepest face leaning towards the plate, degrees from vertical; null when none does) - an area of 0 means it prints without supports at that angle. A face resting on another body still counts. Use layerling_capture_image afterwards to see where the red is.

enabled.description: Switch the red tint on or off. Left out it stays as it is.

angle.description: Steepest overhang the printer manages without supports, degrees from vertical, 30-70.

estimate_print.description: Estimate the material a print needs, like the Material box in the editor's export window: volume, weight and length of 1.75 mm filament, for a solid body (the upper bound) and, in `estimate`, a rough guess with walls and infill as the export window shows it - default 2 walls and 15 % infill; the slicer's own settings decide the real number. Counts what an STL export would hold: visible solid bodies only, groups with their holes taken off, overlapping bodies counted once. Without ids it takes the selection, or the whole design when nothing is selected. Returns volumeMm3, volumeCm3, grams, filamentMeters (all for a solid body), estimate (infillPercent, walls, printedVolumeMm3, grams, filamentMeters with the infill), the material and its density, solids (bodies counted) and unionFailed (overlaps that could not be joined and so count twice).

ids.description: Objects to weigh. Left out: the selection, or the whole design.

material.description: Filament for the weight, default pla (1.24 g/cm3); pa is nylon.

add_reference_points.description: Mark reference points - bare marks in space that shapes snap to when they are dragged, like pencil marks and layout points in a workshop. They are not part of any body, are never printed or exported, and are saved with the design. Mark the centre, the four corners or the four edge middles of objects (on their top face), or pass exact positions with `points`. Points already marked are not added twice. Returns the new points with their ids; shapes can then be placed on them with layerling_update_object.

ids.description: Objects to mark. Left out: the selection.

at.description: Where on the objects' top face (their axis-parallel box, several objects as one): the centre, the four corners or the four edge middles. Default center.

x.description: Position along the plate's X, in mm.

z.description: Position along the plate's depth, in mm, positive towards the front. The editor's Y counts the other way (towards the back), so Y = -z.

points.description: Exact positions instead of marking objects.

list_reference_points.description: List the reference points of the design: id, x, z and elevation in mm.

remove_reference_points.description: Delete reference points by id, or all of them when no ids are given.

ids.description: Points to delete. Left out: all reference points.

show_workplane.description: Show or hide the plate with its grid, labels and any workplane set on a face, like the eye over a grid in the editor's camera bar. Only the view changes: new shapes still land on the workplane, and nothing is saved with the design. Hide it before layerling_capture_image with view "bottom" to see the underside, for example with layerling_show_overhangs. Call without visible to read the state. Returns visible.

visible.description: true shows the plate, false hides it. Left out it stays as it is.

set_section_view.description: Cut the view open along a plane to look inside: walls, cavities, threads in their nuts, parts fitting into each other. Only the view is cut; the design and every export stay whole. Call with no settings to read the current state. axis uses the editor's own coordinates, the same as an object's x, z and elevation: "x" cuts across left-right (offset is an x position), "z" across front-back (a z position), "y" horizontally (offset is a height above the plate, like elevation). The editor's panel names them like its position fields instead: X, Y for the depth (z here) and Z for the height (y here). Switching on, changing the axis or center: true puts the plane in the middle of the design unless offset is given. By default the part on the far side of the plane (greater x, z or height) stays visible; flipped shows the other side. Returns the settings and the plane's useful range (min, max, center). Combine with layerling_capture_image to see the cut.

enabled.description: Switch the section view on or off.

offset.description: Position of the plane in millimetres along the axis.

center.description: Move the plane to the middle of the design.

flipped.description: Show the other side of the plane.

showPlane.description: Draw the blue plane (false hides it, the cut stays).

cutFace.description: How the cut face looks, like the panel's "Cut face": hatch = filled and hatched like a drawing, a body inside another hatched the other way (the start); fill = filled plain, a little darker than the body; open = not filled, you look into the skin of the body. The choice is kept in this browser for every design and returned as cutFace.

orientation.description: What axis and offset are measured along, like the panel's "Axes from": world = the design's axes (default); workplane = the workplane's own axes, offset counted from its origin, "y" cuts parallel to it and the cut moves with the workplane; view = the current view, "y" faces the screen and takes away what lies in front - the view is taken when this is given, so give it again after turning the view. Choosing workplane or view starts on "y" in the middle of the design.

set_history_view.description: Look back at an earlier state of the project, like the editor's History view: the workplane shows that state while the real design stays untouched. Give `index` (0 is the oldest state, the last one is the current design) to open the view at that state or move it, `open: false` to close it, or no settings to read where it stands. While it is open, tools that change the design answer with an error - close it first; reading, `layerling_capture_image` (a picture of the shown state) and the section view still work. `layerling_read_scene` keeps describing the live design. Returns the state shown, how many there are and its bodies; a group lists its `parts` at every depth, whose ids `layerling_restore_from_history` takes. Every answer also has undoStep and redoStep: what undo and redo would take back or bring again from the design's own state, as a sentence with the measure in brackets where the step has one ("Rounded the edges of Box (5 mm)"); lastStep and nextStep carry measures the same way. With `steps: true` it also lists every state with the step that led to it (`steps`, newest last), as the History view's list does.

open.description: false closes the view; true (or an index) opens it.

index.description: The state to show, 0 = oldest. Clamped to the existing states.

steps.description: true adds `steps`: every state's index with the step that led to it, as a sentence.

export_section_svg.description: Cut the design with a plane and return the outlines as an SVG at 1:1 in millimetres - the editor's "Section as SVG". Same bodies as the export: visible solids only, holes already taken off, groups combined, bodies of one colour joined; one unfilled path per body in its colour. An x cut is seen from the right, y from above, z from the front (seenFrom). axis and offset (an x position, a height or a z position, like layerling_set_section_view) default to the current section view, or the middle of the design on that axis; the section view itself is left as it is. Without axis and offset it follows a section view turned to the workplane or the view (orientation in layerling_set_section_view). Returns svg, loops, openLoops (should be 0), widthMm, heightMm and hiddenSkipped. Fails with a message when the plane misses every visible solid.

axis.description: Cutting axis. Defaults to the axis of the section view.

offset.description: Where the plane cuts, in mm: an x position, a height above the plate or a z position. Defaults to the section view's position, or the middle of the design.

save_project.description: Use a Desktop workspace path. Saving a new path is create-only.

set_workplane.description: Set, reset or hide the workplane. A workplane on a face of a body makes new shapes land on that face (layerling_create_shape places onto it), and rotating turns about its normal - the editor's W and a click. id with face puts it on that side of the object's own box, snapped to the real face and centred on it; a face standing up keeps the sketch's up pointing up. flip: true turns it to face inwards. reset: true puts it back on the base plate. visible: false hides a face workplane without dropping it - it still applies, only the drawing goes, which gives a clear view or picture; visible: true shows it again. Setting a new workplane shows it again by itself. Call with no settings to read the state; layerling_read_scene reports it as workplane.

id.description: Object whose face takes the workplane.

face.description: Side of the object's own box, taken in its current turn. Defaults to top.

flip.description: Let the workplane face into the object instead of out of it.

onSection.description: Put the workplane on the cut of the section view (layerling_set_section_view must have it switched on), facing out of the body that stays; a sketch started there shows the outline of the cut.

reset.description: Put the workplane back on the base plate.

visible.description: Show (true) or hide (false) a workplane set on a face.

capture_image.description: Capture a PNG image of the editor viewport from current/home/top/bottom/front/back/right/left view, or from an edge or corner of the view cube by joining neighbouring faces with "-" ("front-right", "top-front", "front-right-top"). By default it is the screen as the user sees it, handles and selection frame included. clean: true gives the picture the editor's export saves as "PNG": only the bodies, at twice the resolution, without handles, selection frames or guides; plate and transparent then choose whether the build plate shows and whether the background is left out.

face.description: current, home, a face, or two or three neighbouring faces joined with "-" for an edge or a corner view, like "front-right-top".

clean.description: Only the bodies, as the PNG export saves them. Implied by plate or transparent.

plate.description: With clean: show the build plate and grid (default true).

transparent.description: With clean: leave the background out (default false).

open_project.description: Use a Desktop workspace path. Saving a new path is create-only.

import_model.description: Use a Desktop workspace path. Saving a new path is create-only.

export_model.description: Export to a Desktop path; existing files cause a conflict.
